sections.title: Strengths
sections.content:
- Can provide the Bible in their local language
- Portuguese -language liturgical alignment
- Portuguese Speaking servants
- Pope Shenouda III mission legacy
- Exceptional History in attracting young men and children to the church
- Flexibility in Resource Allocation
- A Coptic parish offering structured sacramental records
- Ability to Combine Service + Sustainability
- Good fluency and profession in English and French languages
- Ability to Use Simple Digital Tools Effectively
- Ability to Combine Online / Offline Models
- Familiarity with the diseases they are facing
- Ability to Work Through Informal Networks
- Experience in creating Awareness
- The presence of church farms in Egypt

sections.title: Weaknesses
sections.content:
- Limited Portuguese Digital Content
- Unfamiliarity with the country’s traditions
- There are no previous Coptic missions to this country
- There is no sister church in the country
- There are no local Coptic clergy
- Cost Inefficiency for Travel & Logistics
- High single-parenthood creates financial strain on community giving
- Low income, high need for jobs and Limited job

sections.title: Opportunities
sections.content:
- Very large sector of youth
- Ability to Build Deep Personal Relationships
- Church-Based Entry Model
- Education Gap (Learning Crisis)
- Limited Healthcare Awareness
- Weak civil registration
- Simple Lifestyle (Leve Leve)
- High Poverty = High Need for Services
- Small Economy = Easy Influence
- The presence of many catholic churches in the capital
- Growing Internet Penetration (~61.5%), high mobile usage 64%
- ⁠Rapid growth of internet access and social media access
- The outbreaks of many diseases, Weak health services and lack of resources - NGOs for medical
- Political Openness to External Support
- Multiparty System
- Adopting climate -smart agriculture.
- International Support (UNDP / World Bank)
- Focus on Renewable Energy & Sustainability
- Their need to import food supplies
- Water Issues (Quality & Supply)
- High tourism potential due to natural beauty and eco-tourism sites like Príncipe Island
- Open Investment Environment and Tax Incentives & Support
- OIF / Lusophone institutional ties

sections.title: Threats
sections.content:
- High Interest Rates (~10%)
- Weak Infrastructure
- Digital Inequality (Urban vs Rural)
- Land Concession System
- No Registered Entity Yet & Registration Requirements
- Political Instability
- High immigration rates
- Polygamous household structures create canon law conflict at scale
- Extreme female poverty may trigger dependency rather than discipleship
- Visa and residency constraints for clergy
- Catholic Church institutional resistance
